problem: On R2R VLN, strong prior agents (Speaker-Follower, Self-Monitoring) get high success rates only with beam search, which explores many trajectories and produces very long paths (SPL ≈ 0.01–0.02). Greedy-decoding agents keep paths short but have much lower success rates, and they have no way to notice a wrong move and undo it.
motivation: Beam search is unrealistic for a physical robot, since it would have to walk many candidate trajectories, and the SPL metric penalises long paths. The authors view VLN as search over the navigation graph. They observe that the Self-Monitoring agent's progress monitor falls or stalls when the agent deviates from the instruction and rises when it progresses. So the monitor can act as a learned heuristic for best-first-style action selection and backtracking, instead of serving only as a training regulariser or a beam-search scorer.
key_idea: Use the progress monitor's per-step change as a learned heuristic that drives an end-to-end learned rollback decision (Regret Module), and mark visited viewpoints with their progress estimates (Progress Marker) so that after backtracking the greedy agent picks a better direction.
insight: The gain comes from learning when to backtrack, not from better grounding. In the no-augmentation ablation (Table 2, val-unseen), the Regret Module alone lifts greedy Self-Monitoring from 44 SR / 30 SPL to 47 / 37. The Progress Marker alone gives only 44 SR / 32 SPL, and simply appending the progress estimate to the forward embedding gives just 45 SR. The two modules combined reach 48 SR / 37 SPL. Blocking rollback at test time drops Regretful's val-unseen SR 48→46, OSR 61→55 and raises NE 5.36→5.80, while Self-Monitoring's SR is unchanged at 44. SPL, however, rises to 0.41, so rollback trades some path efficiency for success. Trained on synthetic Speaker data only, Regretful beats Self-Monitoring by 41 vs 35 SR, which indicates the search behaviour itself transfers.
method: Baseline Self-Monitoring agent: LSTM instruction encoder, visual-textual co-grounding with soft attention over panoramic ResNet-152 features of navigable directions, an LSTM decoder, and a progress monitor that regresses normalised progress from the textual attention weights plus a gated hidden state (tanh output).

Regret Module: forward embedding m^f = W_a[h_t, x̂_t]; rollback embedding m^r = g(v_{t,r}), the projected visual feature of the direction back to the previous viewpoint. A softmax over W_r·Δp^pm_t (progress change since the last step, detached from the graph) gives forward/rollback weights, and the weighted sum m^fr is used as the movement vector. This acts as a learned, soft replacement for a hand-set threshold.

Action selection: logits are the inner product of W_fr·m^fr with the projected features of each navigable direction, followed by a softmax. After a rollback, the action that would cause oscillation is hard-blocked.

Progress Marker: a memory keyed by viewpoint ID stores the latest progress estimate for each visited location (unvisited = 1, stop = 0). The difference Δv^marker = p^pm_t − marker is tiled n=32 times and concatenated to each direction's visual feature, so visited, low-progress directions become less likely to be chosen.

Training: cross-entropy on the ground-truth action plus MSE on progress (λ=0.5), and an entropy bonus (β=0.01) that encourages exploration and mistakes during training so the agent learns to roll back. Training uses categorical sampling; inference uses pure greedy decoding with no beam search.
Optional data augmentation with Speaker-Follower synthetic instructions (the Regretful* model).

setting.backbone: LSTM seq2seq Self-Monitoring agent with co-grounding attention, progress monitor, Regret Module and Progress Marker (trained from scratch) on frozen ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-152 features

setting.observation: panoramic RGB (ResNet-152 features per navigable direction + 4-d heading/elevation orientation feature)
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (panoramic navigable directions + stop; rollback = moving back to the previous viewpoint)

results: With greedy decoding, Regretful* reaches 48 SR / 40 SPL / 5.69 NE (TL 13.69) on the R2R test server. That is +5 SR and +8 SPL over greedy Self-Monitoring (43/32), and it also beats RCM (43/35). On val-unseen it reaches 50 SR / 41 SPL, and 48 SR / 37 SPL without augmentation. Beam-search Speaker-Follower and Self-Monitoring get higher test SR (53/61) but SPL of only 0.01/0.02, because their trajectories run 1257/373 m.
limitations: Backtracking is only local, one step back to the previous viewpoint, with a hard-coded oscillation block; there is no frontier or global search, and the paper leaves this to future work.

Failure cases show the agent often rolls back correctly but then fails to stop at the goal, so stopping remains a bottleneck. The method also depends on how reliable the progress monitor is, and wrong rollbacks happen at dead ends.
Evaluated only on R2R in the discrete nav-graph setting with ResNet-152 features; rollback can lengthen paths somewhat (blocking rollback raises val-unseen SPL from 0.37 to 0.41).
builds_on: Speaker-Follower (panoramic action space, synthetic data augmentation)
